title: Relationlessness
description: The originating predication cell φ* = (X, p*, R) where X is the entity 'relationlessness' (the would-be configuration name as an entity), p* is the predicate 'has-no-relation', and R is the entity 'relating-locus'. The Leibniz answer: configurational absence does not exist as a separate slot; the would-be absence IS this directed asymmetric cell. Subject-coordinate X and object-coordinate R are structurally distinct — the directional asymmetry every subsequent cell inherits via the four canonical predicate-category morphism classes. Distinct from void, which is the bilattice-bottom value (a value, not a cell).
